components.css: .ds-pipe { min-width: 180px; font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-pipe-bars { display: flex; gap: 4px; } .ds-pipe-bars span { flex: 1; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #e2e4ea; } .ds-pipe-bars .ds-done { background: #121a2c; } .ds-pipe-bars .ds-now { background: #c8102e; animation: ds-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 50% { opacity: 0.5; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-pipe-bars .ds-now { animation: none; } } .ds-pipe-label { margin: 6px 0 0; font-size: 13px; color: #3f4759; } .ds-pipe-label span { color: #5f6678; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
The app is a Vietnamese tear-off wall calendar. Each day the student gets one sheet: a weekday line under a double rule, one huge red numeral for the cards due, and a single red button. Rating a card tears that sheet off the block and shows the next one. Teachers work in the same paper-and-ink world, with an ink-navy rail for classes and a quiet table of lectures moving through the pipeline.

The ground is crisp paper white, not cream. Text is blue-black ink. Lịch red is the calendar's "today" red, and it marks what is due, current, or wrong. Rank comes from weight and case, not from size jumps: tracked uppercase sheet heads, bold titles, and regular body text, all in Be Vietnam Pro. The only big type is the condensed numeral, which carries the calendar's date or the count of cards due.

Interfaces are dense where teachers need them, on laptops, and calm on phones, where students review in short sessions. Depth is physical: a sheet sits on a block of sheets, and nothing else floats.
keyCharacteristics: Paper white ground, blue-black ink, lịch red as the single signal color.
Double hairline sheet rule under every page or sheet head.
Perforated top edge on calendar sheets, plus the logo mark.
Barlow Condensed bold for calendar numerals only; Be Vietnam Pro for everything else.
Tear-off motion when a review card is rated.

rules.name: The Today Red Rule
rules.body: Red means due, today, current, or wrong. Do not use it for decoration, and do not use it for success.

rules.name: The Green Is Done Rule
rules.body: Green appears only once something is finished or correct. A day with nothing left to review turns its sheet green.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Rank is carried by weight and case on a tight scale (12, 13, 15, 28px). Do not add intermediate display sizes. The numeral is the only exception.

rules.name: The Numerals Only Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed sets numbers only: dates, counts, and scores. Never use it for words. The single exception is the one-letter logo mark.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is tabular (`tnum` is on globally) so counts and dates line up.

rules.name: The Sheet Head Rule
rules.body: Every page and every sheet opens with its title over a 3px double ink rule (`border-bottom: 3px double`). This is the calendar sheet head, and it replaces boxed headers.

rules.name: The Only Sheets Lift Rule
rules.body: If it isn't a calendar sheet, it doesn't get a shadow. Cards, tables, and panels use a hairline.

dos: Do open every page and sheet with a title over the 3px double ink rule.
Do show the day's one number in Barlow Condensed bold red. Use a single hero numeral per screen.
Do keep red for due, today, current, or wrong, and green for done or correct.
Do use the perforated edge and sheet-lift shadow only on calendar sheets.
Do give every pressable the 0.97 press scale, and give every animation a reduced-motion fallback.
Do use the 2px red focus outline with a 2px offset (globally on `:focus-visible`).
Do use lucide line icons at 16px for actions, with an `aria-label` on icon-only buttons.
donts: Don't build stat-card dashboards, progress rings, or KPI tiles. Show progress as a pipeline bar, a count, or a sheet.
Don't use cream or warm-tinted grounds. The paper is crisp white (#fdfdfb).
Don't set words in Barlow Condensed, and don't add display sizes between 28px and the numeral.
Don't give flat surfaces (tables, forms, lists) a shadow. Use a hairline.
Don't use typographic glyphs (●, →) as icons or status markers. Use a lucide icon or plain text.
